g.text: Verify - checking the marks a file already carries
resolve the language from the existing mark titles
it is this tool's own lead-in entry?
There is no phrase behind it and never was -
it covers whatever precedes the first
announcement. Reported, it would add a line
saying nothing to every summary of every
book this tool has ever marked.
It may be this file's prologue, epilogue or
--custom mark, and whether the phrase behind
it is really spoken there is exactly as
answerable as a chapter's. What it is not is
a gap boundary - so the outcome recorded
and gap building goes on skipping it.
the title carries a parseable number?
look for that exact chapter number
A skipped mark is still recorded - as
unconfirmed with no number - so it cannot
split a run of unconfirmed marks around it
record the outcome, in file order
A --verify-only run whose marks all fail is a
reports an error and nothing else; the finding
belongs in the output, and a script that wants
group the unconfirmed marks into recovery regions
The confirmed marks are seeded as known, and
each region built around the unconfirmed ones
gets its own Probe - plus the ordinary Scan
a trailing fallback goes with them: nothing
bounds a still-missing trailing chapter from
above, so the gap search structurally cannot
hand them to a gap-scoped detection run
